specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector Phase controls remain usable within both supported viewport widths; Group-color inheritance is reversible, unavailable for Ungrouped Transactions, and does not create History before Apply.
specReviews.reason: The test combines a real Group-color interaction with a compact Inspector fit invariant at two widths; this cross-panel UI contract is not established by a unit test.

specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector and Bottom Phases controls share one unapplied draft and one Apply creates a single History unit.
specReviews.reason: This is a distinct cross-surface Draft/Apply production journey; unit state tests alone cannot prove both editors show the same draft.

specReviews.primaryContract: Multiple Bottom row edits commit together through Apply as one Undoable semantic operation, while rejected Apply leaves Canonical/History unchanged and explains the validation failure.
specReviews.reason: This protects the actual table editing boundary plus command/history outcome; lower-level tests should complement but not replace the visible Apply journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction table headers remain readable/aligned with the body, color is represented in the Color column, and the table fits both supported viewports without page overflow.
specReviews.reason: The two viewport variants directly protect responsive table width and typography, which is an explicit width-dependent visual contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Visible icon-only controls expose accessible names/tooltips and menu/dialog actions expose their interaction semantics across Cycle, Transaction, and Combined; hover help is view-only.
specReviews.reason: This cross-mode accessibility and command-affordance matrix is a distinct UI contract. It currently inspects the rendered control surface directly; retain it while cheaper independent coverage is assessed, not as a duplicate of keyboard navigation tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Visible interactive controls communicate pointer/editability and disabled state consistently across Cycle, Transaction, and Combined.
specReviews.reason: The suite asserts cursor and disabled-reason affordances, a different invariant from accessible naming and mode-specific keyboard undo/redo. Viewport variants are retained pending measured runtime and compact-layout coupling review.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction and Annotation drags visibly explain Escape cancellation, clear the hint after cancellation/release, and preserve Canonical/History on cancel.
specReviews.reason: A real pointer gesture is required to verify the transient status feedback and cancel/release lifecycle; the two Transaction viewport cases guard responsive gesture hit targets.

specReviews.primaryContract: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo one semantic edit consistently in Cycle, Transaction, and Combined.
specReviews.reason: The three modes have distinct command surfaces and the user-visible keyboard route is the contract; this is one parameterized journey per mode, not viewport duplication.

specReviews.primaryContract: Disabled Bottom Transaction commands explain why they are unavailable.
specReviews.reason: This is the specific Transaction Bottom command state, complementary to the cross-mode disabled-cursor audit and suitable for a focused user-visible gate.

specReviews.primaryContract: Ribbon menu, dialog, and immediate actions remain visually/semantically distinguishable at desktop and compact widths.
specReviews.reason: The two viewports are intentional because ribbon density and overflow can alter the visible affordance distinction at compact width.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom Start sort direction changes only view order, preserves selection-independent canonical/history state, and returning to document order restores the original row sequence.
specReviews.reason: This overlaps the broader #747 Start/End sort matrix but uniquely asserts restoring exact document row order; keep this invariant until it is merged into the domain contract suite.

specReviews.primaryContract: Click/Ctrl/Shift/Ctrl+A operate on the Bottom row selection set without checkboxes; Duplicate acts on the selected set as one History unit and Undo restores the original count.
specReviews.reason: This exercises bulk mutation and one-step undo in addition to selection grammar, unlike the selection-only compact journey; preserve both contracts.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom grid supports click/Ctrl/Shift selection, visible-order ranges under filtering, Ctrl+A scoped away from text inputs, and accessible selected/disclosure state without Canonical/History changes.
specReviews.reason: Retain one compact viewport for viewport-independent selection semantics; the removed desktop duplicate is mapped in qa/test-consolidation-map.json and responsive geometry remains tested at both viewports by #747 geometry acceptance.

specReviews.primaryContract: Start/End ascending/descending are announced accessibly, one sort key is active, sorting preserves selected ID and view-only state, and the Bottom settings gear opens/closes with Escape.
specReviews.reason: This is broader than #737's Start-only sorting contract and adds End sorting/settings accessibility. One compact viewport is enough for these semantic assertions; two-view responsive geometry remains in the dedicated #747 geometry acceptance.

specReviews.primaryContract: Follow Selection and Pin are reachable in Bottom settings; Pin changes follow status and survives closing the popover with Escape.
specReviews.reason: A real popover/action journey is needed to verify the production path and persisted view state; the geometry suite measures placement separately.

specReviews.primaryContract: Settings, selection, sort, and Phase expansion preserve the table header position and align child Phase cells with semantic columns at both supported viewport sizes, without document/history changes.
specReviews.reason: The assertions measure responsive panel/header/cell geometry, so both 1280x720 and 1672x941 remain necessary; this suite also replaces the viewport-only geometry coverage removed from semantic tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: During real native horizontal scrolling, Cycle fixed columns stay stationary and visible while the Timeline advances; Canonical, History, and Dirty remain unchanged.
specReviews.reason: This observes the real native scrollbar and user-visible fixed-column behavior at two widths because responsive geometry and native thumb hit area are width-dependent. It replaces the synthetic-width/DOM-ancestry E2E variant while a static architecture guard checks CSS ownership.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Cycle-only scroll split does not shift visible workspace geometry in Cycle, Transaction, or Combined beyond 1px, excluding the documented Cycle-span and Transaction-compression differences.
specReviews.reason: It protects a cross-mode geometry compatibility contract against a hand-authored pre-split reference at both approved viewport sizes; it is layout-specific and belongs outside the ordinary focused PR journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: During real horizontal scrolling, no time-domain pixels intrude beneath the fixed Cycle columns and the timeline scrollbar remains aligned with the time-domain region.
specReviews.reason: This is a distinct pixel-level no-bleed visual contract with screenshot sampling during the drag at both width-dependent layouts; keep it in the visual tier rather than duplicating it in semantic PR tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Analytic LocalGeometry returns the same cycle-boundary, transition, threshold, edge, and value-start anchors as the independent WaveDrom SVG extractor across representative signal tokens and rebased windows.
specReviews.reason: This browser probe is needed to compare two independently produced geometry maps (analytic production source versus real WaveDrom SVG extraction); pure unit tests cannot prove parity with the renderer. It subsumes the narrower cycle-only equivalence spec without duplicating the production pitch formula.

specReviews.primaryContract: Mixed Bookmark, mode-switch, edit, undo/redo, zoom, and cycle operations never navigate away, blank the app, or emit uncaught errors across five deterministic seeds.
specReviews.reason: The five-seed, 36-operation-per-seed randomized lifecycle sweep is diagnostic stress coverage, not a routine PR journey. Keep it automated in nightly; runtime has not been separately measured, so do not infer it from the 240-step count.

specReviews.primaryContract: Repeated Bookmark gestures classify navigation, crash, and opaque-overlay failures immediately with a deterministic action trace.
specReviews.reason: This three-seed repeated Bookmark-only harness provides failure triage evidence beyond the single-per-mode PR journey. Its 24 rounds per test (80 under STRESS753=1) makes it stress coverage; exact runtime remains unmeasured and is explicitly left null.

specReviews.primaryContract: After a real 10,000-cycle document far-scroll, the actual rendered waveform surface bounds cover the timeline viewport.
specReviews.reason: This large-document user-visible geometry journey is expensive and protects viewport coverage after a far jump; its assertion measures the rendered SVG/Canvas surface rectangle rather than internal inline left/width values.

specReviews.primaryContract: A single far jump on a 6,000-cycle Combined document adds no more than the accepted bounded number of waveform batches and leaves rendered waveform owners available.
specReviews.reason: This checks work-count and renderer availability under a large-document far jump, not only visual geometry. It belongs in the performance gate rather than every focused PR run; runtime is pending a measured run.

specReviews.primaryContract: Once Cycle mode reports ready, render counters and ruler/frozen-column/wave-owner/tick geometry remain stable through deferred animation frames.
specReviews.reason: The product contract is post-ready visual stability; the spec measures representative rendered geometry and deferred settling rather than implementation ancestry. Keep it in visual validation, separate from ordinary semantic tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Twenty-one timeline positions during sustained scroll keep waveform owners rendered without increasing WaveDrom render count or changing History.
specReviews.reason: This protects a no-rerender performance invariant across a real scroll sequence; it directly reads renderer counters and is therefore a performance/architecture sentinel rather than a regular product E2E journey. Runtime remains unmeasured.

specReviews.primaryContract: After repeated far/stepped/native-scroll/zoom returns to scrollLeft zero, ruler source origin remains cycle zero and aligned to the waveform origin.
specReviews.reason: This seven-case stress matrix includes 100,000-cycle input, native scrollbar-thumb interaction, and three zoom variants; it must remain automatically executable but not inflate the normal PR path. Its exact runtime is not yet measured on this branch.

specReviews.primaryContract: Real wheel bursts and native scrollbar-thumb drags preserve ruler origin, rendered-window coverage, and view-only state on SVG and Canvas renderers.
specReviews.reason: Renderer-specific real-input paths are distinct from the programmatic rebase matrix, but repeated gestures are stress coverage. Preserve it in nightly; exact runtime is pending measurement.

specReviews.primaryContract: Repeated deterministic right-to-left rebase sequences keep ruler origin, visible source tick, rendered-window coverage, and canonical/history state consistent across SVG/Canvas and short/long documents.
specReviews.reason: It complements real-input scroll coverage with deterministic repeatable window and renderer combinations. Twenty rebases per case are stress workload, so keep it in the automated nightly tier; exact runtime is pending measurement.

specReviews.primaryContract: Editing one Bottom Transaction field makes that cell visibly distinct as an unapplied draft, leaves untouched fields clean, and Escape restores the committed appearance without a semantic edit.
specReviews.reason: The acceptance is a visible dirty-cell affordance plus a native double-click editing gesture. A lower-level test cannot prove that the real editor styles the changed field and restores it on Escape; the spec's data-draft-dirty selector is an implementation-coupled diagnostic and should be paired with computed visual-state assertions.

specReviews.primaryContract: Escape reverts the active Bottom Transaction draft before leaving edit state and does not add History.
specReviews.reason: The ordering between the real focused input, draft reset, and edit lifecycle is user-visible and complements the combined keyboard journey's tab-order check; retain the narrow behavior guard.

specReviews.primaryContract: Keyboard-only F2 editing, left-to-right Tab order, uncommitted draft state, and Escape cancellation work in the dense Bottom grid.
specReviews.reason: The Tab-order assertion is explicitly tied to visible column order and the compact viewport can expose clipping/focus regressions. Both approved widths are retained for this width-sensitive keyboard journey; its compact case also subsumes the standalone F2 smoke via the consolidation map.

specReviews.primaryContract: Left Tree Add creates one stable Transaction visible in Tree, Timeline and Bottom with one History unit; More does not reflow the pane; keyboard traversal skips the removed Signals switch.
specReviews.reason: This combines a real semantic create with stable-ID cross-surface projection and responsive header/focus behavior. Both viewport variants protect the panel's width-sensitive density and are not reducible to an isolated command test.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Transaction Tree exposes named Add, More, Search and Filter controls without a duplicate Signals switch; its Add Group menu action closes correctly and commits one History unit.
specReviews.reason: The Add Group semantic action and one-step History outcome are not covered by the broader Add Transaction/focus journey. The menu DOM checks are surface-level; retain this compact actionable contract while the separate geometry matrix covers width parity.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction Tree control dimensions match Cycle where required; the named menu supports Escape/focus return, view-only Expand/Collapse All, and semantic Show/Hide All.
specReviews.reason: It protects explicit Cycle/Transaction geometry parity at both accepted viewport sizes together with distinct disclosure and visibility semantics. Those width assertions are the reason to retain both variants; menu presence alone overlaps the header smoke but not its state behavior.

specReviews.primaryContract: The row menu nests destinations beneath Move to Group and New Group plus moving the Transaction is a single undoable semantic batch.
specReviews.reason: The menu hierarchy is a user-visible interaction contract and the second journey verifies one-step create+move/undo/redo through the real UI. No existing unit proves both wiring and history grouping.

specReviews.primaryContract: Phase editing exposes parent context, sticky Apply/Revert and coverage validation; stable Phase identity survives Start-order projection while edits/deletes target the intended Phase.
specReviews.reason: The two cases cover complementary user-visible layout/draft validation and stable-identity behavior after display sorting. A model test cannot prove the editor presentation or that row actions resolve the correct canonical Phase.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom search and an unapplied Transaction draft survive primary selection changes, restore by stable Transaction identity, and Escape reverts without Canonical/History changes.
specReviews.reason: This tests a distinct inline Transaction draft and search state across primary selection changes. The Phase-retention suite covers a different editor/domain and cannot replace this lifecycle contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Tree and center Group disclosure controls share view-only state across Transaction and Combined without changing Canonical, History or Dirty state.
specReviews.reason: The contract crosses two rendered surfaces and a mode transition; a lower-level owner test alone cannot prove the visible controls stay synchronized.

specReviews.primaryContract: Unapplied Phase drafts remain visible and recoverable by stable Transaction ID across selection, explicit discard clears them, and New/Open document replacement drops drafts even when IDs repeat.
specReviews.reason: The compact viewport retains all state-lifecycle assertions; the removed desktop copy made no geometry or responsive-layout assertion. The separate New-document case remains because document epoch reset is a distinct contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Logical keyboard navigation remains valid across virtualized row windows and topology/filter changes; mounted rows remain bounded on 520/3,000 Transaction documents.
specReviews.reason: All five cases initialize large production documents and perform long keyboard or bounded-DOM journeys. They remain automated in the heavy integration/performance tiers, not the ordinary PR profile; retain all behavioral cases because row-window keyboard semantics cannot be inferred from a small smoke test.

specReviews.primaryContract: Filtering and Ctrl+A operate on visible Transaction rows only; a destructive bulk Delete cannot affect rows pruned from filtered selection.
specReviews.reason: The destructive-scope guarantee spans actual filter, multi-select, keyboard and Delete UI actions. It is a distinct data-safety contract and should remain in fast PR feedback.

specReviews.primaryContract: Ten thousand Transactions distributed over one hundred individually small Groups still activate global Tree row virtualization and keep mounted rows/DOM bounded.
specReviews.reason: This is the complementary many-small-groups fixture that catches per-Group thresholds missed by a single large-group keyboard case. Preserve it as automated performance/nightly acceptance rather than running it on every PR.

specReviews.primaryContract: Cycle and Transaction remember independent Bottom tabs through repeated Combined round trips, with no Canonical/History changes.
specReviews.reason: The state is view-only but its ownership and restoration are only observable across real mode/tab navigation; this is a compact representative cross-mode journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: Global and per-Group Hide All preserve the existing selected stable ID; the next destructive command still targets only that selection.
specReviews.reason: Global Hide All additionally tests the scope of the subsequent Delete, while per-Group Hide All independently protects selection ownership. Both real command paths are retained; the fixture is small and unrelated to the filter-scope issue.

specReviews.primaryContract: Clock Generator Apply and Inspector Convert Clock actions remain reachable without scrolling at both supported viewport sizes.
specReviews.reason: This is specifically a vertical reachability/viewport-fit contract, so both heights are meaningful and the real rendered controls must be measured in a browser.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Annotation Bottom remains list-first and scrollable; row selection and preview drafts stay view-only until Apply; Inspector Apply/Undo/Redo and creation keep the collection synchronized.
specReviews.reason: This combines a long scrollable collection with cross-surface selection and draft/commit semantics. Both viewports test explicit list-first visibility and available vertical room, so they are not semantic duplicates.

specReviews.primaryContract: In Combined mode, selecting a Transaction after a Signal switches Inspector entity context without changing History.
specReviews.reason: The multi-mode context suite does not select a Transaction from the Combined Tree after a Signal, so this small direct user path is complementary rather than duplicated.

specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector projection follows active workspace and restores hidden Transaction/Signal selection by stable identity through Cycle/Transaction/Combined without data or History changes.
specReviews.reason: The cross-mode stable selection lifecycle is a distinct owner contract. Its desktop duplicate was removed because neither test asserts viewport geometry; the compact test retains the complete journey and error check.

specReviews.primaryContract: The titlebar keeps document name distinct from active Cycle/Transaction/Combined view and remains correct after document load and browser reload.
specReviews.reason: The reload and active-view label are production-visible lifecycle behavior. The desktop width copy was redundant because the test checks no width-dependent geometry; the compact case covers all transitions.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transaction time-grid vertical indicators remain neutral, thin, non-interactive and behind Transaction bars.
specReviews.reason: Layering and pointer transparency are visible interaction geometry; computed style/z-order reads are appropriate for this visual acceptance but should not be generalized to semantic tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: Transition End and Duration are non-editable derived outputs, and row toolbar actions visibly identify the selected Transition they affect.
specReviews.reason: Lower-level tests can check derived values, but this browser contract verifies the real table renders them as outputs and scopes actions to the selected row; retain one focused UI guard.

specReviews.primaryContract: An untouched Signal Generator is not shown as a user-edited draft; actual editing marks it unapplied and Cancel restores pristine fields without Canonical/History/Dirty changes.
specReviews.reason: The regression distinguishes default form values from user-edited draft state in the live UI, including cancel behavior; a reducer test cannot establish the user-visible affordance.

specReviews.primaryContract: Signal-wide Group move/visibility/delete actions stay in the scoped command group and do not replace the independent Bottom draft Cancel action.
specReviews.reason: This protects command ownership and visible separation between semantic Signal operations and draft lifecycle controls; the browser assertion catches relocation or action collision.

specReviews.primaryContract: Switching selected Signal discards the previous Signal's Add Transition draft rather than leaking values into the next Signal's scope, with no History commit.
specReviews.reason: This is a stable-identity/draft-isolation contract across real Signal selection changes, distinct from the generator's pristine-draft lifecycle.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Signal transition form clearly states whether it will add a new Transition or edit the selected existing Transition.
specReviews.reason: The mode/status text prevents an edit from being mistaken for an add. This concise visible affordance check complements the Transition draft isolation journey.

specReviews.primaryContract: Selection following cannot activate a Bottom tab unavailable in the current mode; active tab and panel content remain mode-compatible across selection changes.
specReviews.reason: This covers selection-following and tab compatibility, distinct from #773's explicit mode round-trip memory contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Creating a Transaction while in Cycle mode changes canonical data once but does not expose or activate Transaction-only Bottom content in the Cycle workspace.
specReviews.reason: This tests creation from a mode that does not own Transaction Bottom content; it complements selection-following by verifying creation itself does not leak a tab.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Transaction Tree's screen position and width remain fixed while the timeline horizontally scrolls, without changing History.
specReviews.reason: This requires actual horizontal overflow and compares screen geometry at both accepted viewport sizes; both variants protect width-dependent geometry rather than duplicate semantic behavior.

specReviews.primaryContract: Selecting an off-screen Transaction minimally reveals its bar, leaves the Tree fixed, and does not alter Canonical/History/Dirty; selecting a visible or already revealed row does not jump again.
specReviews.reason: A 1,000-cycle real document with actual wheel scrolling is necessary to test minimal reveal against near/mid/far bars. Both viewport widths exercise different visible ranges; preserve it for automated integration/nightly, outside routine PR.

specReviews.primaryContract: Both Cancel and Escape close the Bulk Signal Registration dialog and return focus to the stable Add trigger.
specReviews.reason: Cancel and Escape are distinct close paths for focus lifecycle; this parameterized browser case is concise and verifies focus restoration at the real dialog boundary.

specReviews.primaryContract: Dragging a Canvas-rendered Annotation keeps stable identity and synchronizes Inspector/list through Undo/Redo, selection changes and Save/Open at supported viewport sizes.
specReviews.reason: The real-pointer, renderer, history and serialization journey is a release/integration contract. Retain both viewports because rendering/handle geometry vary with available space; exclude this broad flow from routine PR feedback.

specReviews.primaryContract: After horizontal timeline scroll, the Combined divider remains pinned to the visible split edge and real pointer dragging changes pane height without History mutation.
specReviews.reason: This is an actual pointer-resize and pinned-divider geometry contract, distinct from shared horizontal axis alignment. It uses one representative wide viewport and belongs outside routine semantic PR execution.

specReviews.primaryContract: A matching source-cycle ruler boundary and Transaction position share one horizontal mapping in Combined, Cycle vertical scrolling does not move the Transaction pane, and mode round trips remain view-only.
specReviews.reason: The two viewport cases assert width-sensitive shared-axis alignment and pane independence; the separate mode round-trip case protects view-state semantics. This complements the real-wheel #760 owner test and remains an integration/visual contract.

specReviews.primaryContract: Workspace, Bottom, Inspector and status regions retain stable per-mode geometry through Cycle/Transaction/Combined round trips and remain within viewport bounds.
specReviews.reason: This directly guards the Issue's mode-owner isolation contract at both accepted viewport sizes using measured region geometry. It is the focused visual guard needed before any broader CSS ownership extraction.

specReviews.primaryContract: After Cycle/Combined mode transitions, Save, browser reload and Recent restore the complete Signal waveform and stable Annotation projection with clean Canonical/History state.
specReviews.reason: The contract crosses renderer readiness, mode switching, browser reload and persisted Recent document recovery; it belongs in automated integration/nightly coverage. Both viewport sizes remain because rendering projection and available canvas space differ with height.

specReviews.primaryContract: Clearing a selected Transaction restores the Inspector Layout section and selecting it again returns to entity properties without changing History.
specReviews.reason: This is a user-visible selection-clear transition not covered by #629's mode switching or stable-selection restoration. Keep the focused guard while noting its coordinate-based blank-tree click as a candidate for a named production clear-selection control in a later harness review.

specReviews.primaryContract: Inspector section disclosure uses the same chevron glyph and visible size as Tree disclosure controls, and aria-expanded follows the open/close state.
specReviews.reason: This is a compact visual/accessibility consistency assertion over one real disclosure interaction. Icon metadata and box measurements are appropriate for a focused visual profile, not a broad E2E matrix.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom rows, Transaction Tree rows and timeline bars distinguish hover, selection and keyboard focus through their intended visual states.
specReviews.reason: Three surfaces share design tokens but have distinct rendering owners; computed visual states are the acceptance boundary, so this belongs in the focused visual profile rather than semantic PR journeys.

specReviews.primaryContract: At 125% device scale, splitters remain operable, real pointer resize works, key controls meet minimum hit dimensions, and document state remains unchanged.
specReviews.reason: The device-scale factor and two viewport sizes exercise physical-to-CSS hit geometry; the real splitter drag and document invariants are not covered by static/unit checks.

specReviews.primaryContract: Bottom and Inspector splitters expose usable hit areas and resize affordance, preserve user sizing across selection/mode changes, and do not mutate document state.
specReviews.reason: This complements the 125%-scale pointer case by checking both splitter orientations, hover discovery and keyboard sizing across mode round trips; these are separate view-state contracts.

specReviews.primaryContract: Double-clicking either splitter restores its default size without changing History or Dirty state.
specReviews.reason: Reset is a distinct, inexpensive user action with a view-only invariant; one desktop case is sufficient because the behavior is not viewport-specific.

specReviews.primaryContract: Developer-only diagnostics start collapsed and can be deliberately revealed without document mutation, while the left workspace rail does not cover status UI at compact size across modes.
specReviews.reason: The file combines a state disclosure contract with a compact cross-mode layout boundary; both are production-visible and the 1280x720 measurement protects the regression directly.

specReviews.primaryContract: Tree and Bottom transaction searches have explicit scope, active filters are visible, zero-result feedback identifies the query, and view filtering does not change History.
specReviews.reason: This compact UI path validates distinct Tree/Bottom search affordances and the user-visible empty state alongside a view-only history invariant.

specReviews.primaryContract: Hovering a Transaction lane produces a visible lane highlight that helps follow the row across the canvas.
specReviews.reason: The contract is purely visual and checks the actual rendered lane state; a deterministic single viewport is sufficient.

specReviews.primaryContract: Unselected Bookmark markers are visually secondary and gain prominence on hover.
specReviews.reason: This is a separate marker visual hierarchy from lane hover and is appropriately checked as a compact visual contract at the real UI boundary.

specReviews.primaryContract: MiniMap exposes an accessible name and concise interaction hint identifying it as a timeline navigator.
specReviews.reason: The accessibility metadata is a small user-facing affordance contract; a focused DOM/accessibility-boundary assertion is sufficient without a visual matrix.

specReviews.primaryContract: Double-clicking a Transaction Group header collapses/expands its children without invoking rename or changing History.
specReviews.reason: The gesture disambiguation between collapse and rename is a real pointer interaction with a view-only invariant; the single canonical group fixture is adequate.

specReviews.primaryContract: A semantic edit displays an unsaved marker in the document title, and successful Save clears it.
specReviews.reason: The user-visible dirty-to-saved transition crosses the semantic mutation and Save completion boundary; it is a concise high-value PR contract and should not be replaced by a unit-only dirty flag test.

specReviews.primaryContract: At both supported viewport sizes, hiding Bottom returns its space to the Cycle canvas, remains stable through a mode round-trip, restores Bottom on demand, and leaves canonical revision, History and Dirty unchanged.
specReviews.reason: The test asserts user-visible region geometry, hidden/visible state and view-only invariants in the real workspace; this is the single retained guard after removing duplicate variants that repeated the same hide/round-trip/show flow or inspected CSS grid tracks directly.

specReviews.primaryContract: Fit-sized Transaction lanes create no phantom vertical overflow; a real 50-Transaction canonical document has one scroll owner and can reveal its far lane through user wheel input without page scrolling or document mutation.
specReviews.reason: The two viewport cases protect the fit/no-phantom boundary, and one compact tall-document case covers virtual lane reachability through production Open and real wheel interaction. The prior DOM minHeight mutation was removed because it did not prove a tall canonical document.

specReviews.primaryContract: The visible TC scale readout uses singular 'cycle' for one and plural 'cycles' for other supported scale values, without changing its semantic scale behavior.
specReviews.reason: The copy behavior is independent of viewport dimensions; the compact viewport retains the three-value user-visible wording check without a redundant desktop duplicate.

specReviews.primaryContract: The Cycle transition Start input can display multi-digit cycle values at both supported viewport widths without clipping or displacing Value/Comment controls.
specReviews.reason: The measured input width and sibling-boundary check protect a real compact-layout constraint; both viewports are intentional because narrow width can change flex allocation.

specReviews.primaryContract: During real native horizontal scrollbar movement, every Transaction Group context header stays wholly inside the timeline viewport, hit-testable, and returns to its exact resting inset after scrolling back; collapse/expand preserves pinning without document mutation.
specReviews.reason: The pinned-label behavior requires actual horizontal overflow and native scrollbar interaction, then checks viewport and hit-target geometry at desktop and compact widths. It is intentionally excluded from the routine PR profile; its scrollbar-thumb coordinate calculation remains a harness portability risk to revisit separately.

specReviews.primaryContract: Switching Bookmark selection retains an unapplied draft under its original stable entity, announces it, and allows explicit discard without changing History or Canonical revision.
specReviews.reason: This covers the Bookmark-specific selection/draft lifecycle that differs from Transaction Phase and Annotation drafts; it traverses the production panel and includes a console-error guard.

specReviews.primaryContract: Applying the Annotation Anchor commits that sub-editor while preserving a distinct unapplied Label draft for the same stable Annotation.
specReviews.reason: The test protects independence between two Annotation Inspector sub-editors, a concrete production-visible draft boundary not covered by cross-entity retention tests.

specReviews.primaryContract: An unrelated Reset Semantics Apply preserves a Signal Properties draft, and Undo after Clock generator Apply refreshes the Inspector draft to the restored Canonical value.
specReviews.reason: The two cases represent distinct high-risk failure paths—cross-subeditor draft discard and stale local state after Undo—so they remain separate cases within one focused file rather than one broad journey.

reviews.title: large documents paint Canvas without per-cycle SVG; ?wave=svg forces the SVG fallback
reviews.primaryContract: A 30-signal x 10,000-cycle document auto-selects viewport-bounded Canvas rendering without per-cycle SVG node growth, while the supported SVG fallback remains forceable.
reviews.reason: This large fixture checks the renderer budget/selection architecture, not only a visible journey. Keep it automated in the performance and full nightly tiers, outside routine PR feedback; runtime not measured in this audit.

reviews.title: selection, hit-test, zoom, resize and sustained drag on the Canvas path keep the ruler and geometry aligned
reviews.primaryContract: On the production Canvas path, selection and far-window hit testing follow semantic time; zoom, resize, sustained scrolling, and view-only operations preserve ruler alignment and bounded rendered state.
reviews.reason: This is a high-value cross-operation Canvas user journey over a 300k-signal-cycle fixture and 60 scroll steps. Keep the expensive acceptance in integration/nightly rather than replacing it with cheaper unit checks.

reviews.title: annotation anchoring, snap and edge counter resolve on the Canvas path in a far window
reviews.primaryContract: Far-window Canvas coordinates resolve cycle selection, annotation anchoring, snap, and reference-clock edge counters from the shared analytic geometry.
reviews.reason: The browser verifies multiple production consumers agree on the renderer-independent geometry at a far window; the large document makes it inappropriate for routine PR runs.

reviews.title: export of a large Canvas-rendered document still produces SVG from canonical data
reviews.primaryContract: Export from a Canvas-rendered large document still downloads an SVG representation derived from canonical data.
reviews.reason: The renderer choice must not leak into the export format; this full large-document download journey belongs in integration/nightly validation.

reviews.title: memory stays bounded over repeated far jumps (no canvas/DOM/heap leak)
reviews.primaryContract: After warm-up and 24 repeated far-window jumps on a 300k document, Canvas count, DOM growth, and available heap remain bounded.
reviews.reason: This is a 24-round memory/retention stress test, not a functional PR journey. Preserve it in automated performance/nightly runs and measure its runtime in the later cost-baseline phase.

reviews.title: Combined horizontal wheel scrolls the shared viewport at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: In a fresh Combined workspace, horizontal wheel input over either pane advances the one shared time viewport and leaves Canonical/History/Dirty unchanged.
reviews.reason: A real wheel gesture is necessary to distinguish pane-local from shared scroll ownership. The compact-width case exercises both pane input locations; the removed desktop duplicate is mapped in the consolidation file.

reviews.title: zoom does not stretch Transaction text at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At zoom 200/400/800%, Transaction and Phase text retain rendered natural dimensions while track scroll extent and ruler/bar alignment follow layout geometry.
reviews.reason: The test observes text dimensions and ruler/bar alignment rather than asserting that specific CSS transform properties are absent. One compact viewport is sufficient for width-independent glyph scaling.

reviews.title: dragging a Transaction edge at 400% zoom lands on the cycle under the pointer
reviews.primaryContract: A real Transaction edge drag at 400% zoom updates the visible end-time value to the cycle under the pointer and creates a semantic edit.
reviews.reason: Pointer conversion under high zoom requires a real browser gesture; the assertion checks the semantic Inspector result in the current TC display unit instead of reconstructing expected movement from bar pixel width.

reviews.title: a narrow Transaction bar keeps a body drag handle and can be moved
reviews.primaryContract: When TC compression makes a Transaction bar narrow and its name is compacted, the remaining visible body handle supports a real move operation.
reviews.reason: The minimum pointer target and compact label are visual/browser behavior; this journey is distinct from edge resizing at high zoom.

reviews.title: median view-mode switch on a 24x256 document stays inside the budget
reviews.primaryContract: Median in-page mode-switch latency across eight Cycle/Transaction transitions on the fixed 24x256 fixture stays below the explicit 3,000ms budget without changing History.
reviews.reason: This is a measured performance budget, not a functional correctness timeout; keep it in the dedicated performance/nightly gate. Runtime collection remains pending.

reviews.title: Custom TC scale accepts only a positive integer and never applies an invalid draft
reviews.primaryContract: Custom cycles-per-TC accepts a valid positive integer; invalid/empty drafts disable Apply, explain the error, and do not create History.
reviews.reason: The visible custom-input validation and Apply-enabled state belong to the user interaction boundary. Multiple invalid values are table-driven in one journey rather than separate browser cases.

reviews.title: 1 TC = 10 cycles -> 50 cycles compresses bars 5x, keeps TC label pitch, never changes canonical cycles (1280x720)
reviews.primaryContract: The same canonical Transaction span becomes one-fifth the physical width at 50 cycles/TC, TC ruler pitch remains stable, source duration stays unchanged, and Undo restores geometry.
reviews.reason: This is the representative production geometry journey; it measures the relative width change and canonical duration rather than reproducing the transform formula. The duplicate desktop run is mapped to this case; width-specific clipping remains separately tested at both viewports.

reviews.title: compressed Transaction: no clipped labels and no artificial scroll extent at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At compact width, compressed Transaction labels do not clip or disappear and scrollWidth reflects the presented content without artificial overflow.
reviews.reason: The contract is explicitly width-dependent: a narrow bar and compact viewport can expose clipping and false scroll extent not present at desktop size.

reviews.title: compressed Transaction: no clipped labels and no artificial scroll extent at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: At desktop width, compressed Transaction labels do not clip or disappear and scrollWidth reflects the presented content without artificial overflow.
reviews.reason: The desktop counterpart is retained because width changes determine which short bars can display their names and whether the timeline acquires false overflow.

reviews.title: Transaction ruler labels follow cycles-per-TC (10 -> 5 -> 1 -> Undo) and Cycle mode stays in cycles
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction ruler labels and source-cycle boundaries follow 10/5/1 cycles-per-TC, Undo restores the prior scale, and Cycle mode continues to label source cycles.
reviews.reason: The mode-crossing ruler journey protects the shared display-unit contract, complementary to the bar-width/canonical geometry test; known label/source anchors are independent fixture expectations.

reviews.title: Transaction header exposes a cycles-per-TC selector that is one undoable edit
reviews.primaryContract: Changing the header cycles-per-TC selector updates displayed Bottom values while preserving entity identity, and creates exactly one Undoable view-setting history operation.
reviews.reason: This verifies the actual ribbon selector to Bottom projection to Undo path; it is distinct from ruler-label progression and invalid custom draft validation.

reviews.title: ruler cell is the hit target, in Cycle at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Whitespace and vertical positions within Cycle ruler cells select the intended source cell; left-to-right and right-to-left drags select the same view-only range.
reviews.reason: This protects a real pointer hit target and range-selection journey that cannot be proven without the rendered ruler; compact viewport covers this mode's own ruler/time origin. Pointer coordinates are based on adjacent rendered tick spacing, not a copied pitch constant.

reviews.title: ruler cell is the hit target, in Cycle at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Whitespace and vertical positions within Cycle ruler cells select the intended source cell; left-to-right and right-to-left drags select the same view-only range.
reviews.reason: This is the desktop-width counterpart because ruler origin/available cell geometry is width-dependent; it protects the same visible Cycle-mode pointer gesture at the documented full viewport.

reviews.title: ruler cell is the hit target, in Transaction at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Whitespace and vertical positions within compressed Transaction ruler cells resolve through the shared mapping; either drag direction selects the same view-only range.
reviews.reason: Transaction ruler hit testing has a distinct compressed time mapping from Cycle mode, and the compact viewport exercises its own origin/available cells. Coordinates are derived from rendered ruler ticks.

reviews.title: ruler cell is the hit target, in Transaction at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Whitespace and vertical positions within compressed Transaction ruler cells resolve through the shared mapping; either drag direction selects the same view-only range.
reviews.reason: The desktop counterpart protects compressed Transaction ruler hit testing at the full viewport; responsive ruler origin is width-dependent, so this variant remains distinct.

reviews.title: every Bookmark gesture stays inside the SPA in Cycle mode
reviews.primaryContract: Cycle-mode Bookmark create/select/reveal/previous/next/ruler interactions stay in the current SPA with the editor mounted and no uncaught errors.
reviews.reason: P0 user-visible navigation guard across the actual in-app Bookmark entry points; the Cycle mode case cannot be proven by pure or component tests. One viewport is used because this invariant is independent of width.

reviews.title: every Bookmark gesture stays inside the SPA in Transaction mode
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction-mode Bookmark create/select/reveal/previous/next/ruler interactions stay in the current SPA with the editor mounted and no uncaught errors.
reviews.reason: P0 guard for the mode in which the blank-screen report occurred; the full production gesture path and mode-specific navigation viewport require a browser. Kept at a single width because navigation is width-independent.

reviews.title: every Bookmark gesture stays inside the SPA in Combined mode
reviews.primaryContract: Combined-mode Bookmark create/select/reveal/previous/next/ruler interactions stay in the current SPA with the editor mounted and no uncaught errors.
reviews.reason: P0 guard for the shared two-pane viewport path; it verifies the user-visible navigation entry points against Combined ownership. A single viewport is enough for this width-independent navigation invariant.

reviews.title: Annotation Preview Update reverts even without an explicit Cancel, when selection moves away
reviews.primaryContract: A transient annotation preview is removed when selection changes, without mutating canonical state.
reviews.reason: The annotation overlay preview lifecycle is user-visible and owner-specific; the similar Clock test exercises a different renderer and draft owner, so title similarity is not duplicate coverage.

reviews.title: Clock Preview reverts even without an explicit Cancel, when selection moves away
reviews.primaryContract: A transient Clock waveform preview is removed when selection changes, without mutating canonical state.
reviews.reason: The Clock waveform preview uses a distinct renderer and draft owner from annotation overlay preview; keep the independent visible regression journey.

reviews.title: Apply commits the previewed draft as one real SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a previewed Annotation draft commits the same values through one semantic command.
reviews.reason: The visually similar Clock test protects a separate editor and waveform projection; it does not replace Annotation command application coverage.

reviews.title: Apply after Preview commits exactly the previewed draft as one real SemanticCommand
reviews.primaryContract: Applying a previewed Clock draft commits the previewed generator through one semantic command.
reviews.reason: The Annotation counterpart cannot prove Clock waveform preview/application equivalence, so retain both product journeys.

reviews.title: Bottom Editor splitter resizes and collapses without changing document or render state
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom splitter interaction changes panel size/visibility without Canonical, History, Dirty, or render-session changes.
reviews.reason: Inspector resize is a similar gesture but has a different axis, owner, state, and layout consequence; a shared low-level drag unit test would not replace this observable contract.

reviews.title: Inspector splitter resizes and collapses without changing document or render state
reviews.primaryContract: Inspector splitter interaction changes panel width/visibility without Canonical, History, Dirty, or render-session changes.
reviews.reason: Bottom resize differs in orientation and layout owner; keep this as the user-visible inspector-specific journey rather than merging by title similarity.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for small fixture at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Small Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: This is a small-fixture baseline at compact viewport; it differs in fixture size and purpose from the separate 500-Transaction scalability budget test. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for small fixture at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Small Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at desktop viewport.
reviews.reason: Desktop viewport is retained as a responsive/performance comparison against 1280x720; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for medium fixture at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: Medium Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: Medium fixture adds a scale point to the startup curve, not duplicate acceptance of the 500-Transaction case. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: Transaction Open reaches first useful paint for medium fixture at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Medium Transaction document open reaches useful Transaction projection at desktop viewport.
reviews.reason: Desktop viewport is retained as a responsive/performance comparison against 1280x720; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: 500-Transaction Open reaches first useful Transaction paint at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: A large Transaction document produces a non-zero visible bar projection after Open.
reviews.reason: This is the large-scale stress point with its own 500-Transaction fixture and explicit scalability assertions; it is not a duplicate of small/medium startup checks. Runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: 500-Transaction Open reaches first useful Transaction paint at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: A large Transaction document produces a non-zero visible bar projection at compact viewport.
reviews.reason: Compact viewport stresses available workspace and row projection separately from desktop; runtime has not yet been measured.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Cycle: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Cycle mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Representative fresh-state Cycle entry journey; complementary Transaction and Combined entries are also retained in the same product lifecycle contract suite.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Transaction: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Transaction mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Transaction workspace has a separate initialization/projection path, so this user-visible mode entry complements Cycle and Combined smoke journeys.

reviews.title: J1-3 fresh -> Combined: renders, view-only, no errors
reviews.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Combined mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
reviews.reason: Combined composes two view owners and needs its own real startup journey; this is not covered by either single mode.

reviews.title: J4/J16 Cycle -> Transaction -> Combined -> Cycle, then rapid switching, stays view-only and error-free
reviews.primaryContract: Mode transitions and rapid switching preserve document/history state and keep the application error-free.
reviews.reason: This is the direct cross-mode lifecycle invariant and exercises state transitions that static/unit tests cannot fully prove.

reviews.title: J5/J10 select -> edit -> Apply -> Undo -> Redo, and an unapplied draft does not leak to the next selection
reviews.primaryContract: Selection changes discard an unapplied draft; Apply creates one history step and Undo/Redo restore the committed state.
reviews.reason: This production journey covers cross-selection draft isolation plus the visible Apply/Undo/Redo contract, which is not reducible to a single unit invariant.

reviews.title: J9 Bottom follows the selected entity kind
reviews.primaryContract: Bottom panel follows the selected entity kind across the actual application surface.
reviews.reason: The selected entity kind drives a cross-surface panel contract that is appropriately verified at the UI boundary.

reviews.title: Transaction tree selection opens the selected canonical transaction in Inspector
reviews.primaryContract: Selecting a Transaction in the Tree selects that same canonical entity in Inspector and applies edits to it.
reviews.reason: This is the focused Transaction selection/Inspector production route and is a small changed-domain browser journey.

reviews.title: #554 from-scratch Transaction workspace journey at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: Production-path Transaction creation, group/link edits, selection sync, Undo/Redo, mode round trips, and Save/New/Open preserve semantic data.
reviews.reason: This is a broad end-to-end lifecycle with real file save/open and many semantic operations. Keep out of ordinary focused PR verification, but retain as automated integration acceptance.

reviews.title: #554 from-scratch Transaction workspace journey at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: The same production-path Transaction lifecycle remains usable at a compact viewport while semantic edits survive Save/New/Open.
reviews.reason: The journey exercises responsive panel geometry and overflow-sensitive controls at 1280x720; the desktop variant is not a substitute for this width-specific contract.

reviews.title: locks v8 badge, display, MiniMap, and bottom-toolbar geometry
reviews.primaryContract: Role badge/frozen-column alignment, toolbar control grouping, and MiniMap stability remain within approved visual geometry.
reviews.reason: This single desktop geometry contract checks measurable visual relationships rather than a broad screenshot matrix; it belongs in the visual profile, not every semantic PR journey.

reviews.title: #741 Transaction fixed-width sidebar exposes no focusable ghost resizer and hides no width mutation
reviews.primaryContract: Transaction mode has no keyboard-operable fixed-width sidebar separator, while Cycle retains its functional separator.
reviews.reason: This is a concise real keyboard/focus contract for the mode-specific control and is separate from the Cycle rail geometry cases in the same spec file.

reviews.title: #756 Cycle left rail spans Main + Bottom as one column (tree viewport reaches the workspace bottom) at 1672x941
reviews.primaryContract: At both supported viewport sizes, the Cycle Tree reaches the workspace bottom, stays beside rather than under the Bottom table, and the timeline scrollbar remains attached above the Bottom splitter.
reviews.reason: This measures the structural left-rail relationship and scrollbar boundary across both viewport sizes; it complements the #740 bottom-hidden test without repeating its hide/show journey.

reviews.title: #756 Cycle left rail spans Main + Bottom as one column (tree viewport reaches the workspace bottom) at 1280x720
reviews.primaryContract: At both supported viewport sizes, the Cycle Tree reaches the workspace bottom, stays beside rather than under the Bottom table, and the timeline scrollbar remains attached above the Bottom splitter.
reviews.reason: The compact viewport can expose rail clipping and overflow relationships that differ from desktop; retain this width-specific layout acceptance.
